rgb: The scene is an outdoor grassy lawn viewed from a steep downward angle, with no other people present besides the camera wearer. Far below the viewpoint at 3 to 5 metres are the camera wearer's grey shirt, shoulders, and chin, with both arms extended forward and downward so the hands grip a lawnmower handlebar at roughly 4 to 5 metres. The walk-behind lawnmower extends forward in front of the camera wearer from the handlebar at 4.5 metres to the grey grass-catcher bag at about 4.0 to 4.5 metres and the silver deck with a red engine housing at about 3 to 4 metres, while the front edge of the mower deck is partly cut off by the top of each frame. The handlebar is held in both hands well out of arm's reach, and the grass-catcher bag is also out of arm's reach just ahead of the wearer's legs. The camera wearer's torso and the handlebar partially occlude the wearer's black shorts, legs, and alternating shoes directly underneath, while the mower body occludes the patch of grass beneath it. Across the five frames, the relative distance and alignment between the camera wearer and the lawnmower remain nearly constant at roughly 3 to 5 metres ahead as both move away together over the grass with slight right-left shifts and alternating foot positions.
depth: The depth map shows a steep downward egocentric view of an outdoor lawn where the camera wearer (the only person present, facing backward and looking straight down) pulls away from a walk-behind lawn mower across five frames. Dark grey to near-black tones place the wearer's upper torso at 4.6–5.0 m below the head-mounted camera, both extended arms and hands gripping the mower handlebar out of arm's reach at about 4.3–4.5 m in front and below, and the mower's grass catcher bag and engine deck farther away on the ground at roughly 3.0–4.0 m from the camera (3.0–5.0 m ahead of the handlebar). Between the wearer's occluding torso and the handlebar, slightly lighter grey shapes appear in alternating frames (right leg/foot in frames 1, 2, and 5; both knees/feet in frame 3; left leg in frame 4) at 3.3–4.2 m below the camera as the wearer walks backward while maintaining a constant distance to the mower, whose front edge is partly cropped at the top of the frame. Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height gradient from the distant handlebar down the angled support rods to the mower body and ground plane, avoiding texture confusion from the patchy grass and mulch. However, the depth map is unreliable along the thin side cables/rods, which partially vanish into the dark ground depth, and around the flat grass background where subtle ground slopes are compressed into uniform near-black.
segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's torso, arms, hands, and stepping legs at the bottom center (3.3–5.0 m from the camera, facing backward and looking down with no other people present) from the unlabelled black background lawn. Across all five frames, the wearer's right and left hands remain out of arm's reach at 4.3–4.5 m, gripping the mower handlebar directly in front of the torso while the torso occludes most of the lower body except through the gap between the arms and handlebar. As the wearer walks backward with slight lateral sway and a slight rightward turn by frame 5, the map captures the changing shape of the gap between the arms and chest where the stepping legs and handlebar sit, while the top of the mower and bottom of the wearer's head remain partly out of view. While the segmentation mask makes the continuous silhouette boundary of the wearer's upper body and arms easier to see than in RGB, its semantic labels and object detections are highly unreliable under this steep egocentric angle. Specifically, it completely misses the lawn mower in frames 2, 3, and 5, misclassifies the mower deck and grass bag (~3.0–4.0 m ahead) as a "parking meter" and a tiny "person" fragment in frames 1 and 4, merges the handlebar into the "person" mask in frames 2–3, and mislabels the handlebar center as a "cell phone" in frame 5.
pose: The pose map renders only two magenta 2D hand skeletons on a black background, corresponding to the camera wearer's right and left hands positioned out of arm's reach at roughly 4.3–4.5 m in front of and below the downward-looking camera, spaced about 3–5 m apart right-to-left on the mower handlebar. Each hand skeleton shows the wrist at the outer lower corner and five curled fingers wrapping forward and inward around the angled grips, confirming the wearer faces backward behind the mower while no other people are in the scene. Across the five frames, the pair of hand skeletons shifts slightly upward in frames 2–3 and tilts slightly clockwise (right hand higher, left hand lower) in frame 5, tracking the subtle handlebar angle and torso sway as the wearer walks backward. Compared to RGB, the magenta keypoints make the exact finger articulation, thumb placement, and symmetrical grip orientation immediately explicit without visual clutter from the handlebar or grass. However, the map is unreliable for full-body spatial understanding because it completely fails to detect the yellow body skeleton for the wearer's visible shoulders, elbows, torso, and stepping legs—which are heavily foreshortened and self-occluded from the head-mounted viewpoint—and provides no representation of the lawn mower or ground.
